from.place: Proof paragraph 2 of prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint, mapping-complex adjunction infrastructure through lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints, lem-coef-small-saturated-arrow-accessibility and lem-coef-filtered-presentation-common-refinement; HTT Lemma 5.5.4.13, relative lifting construction on printed pp. 479-480; the weak homotopy equivalence Y restricted to N(A_0(n)) into Y on printed p. 480

title: A colimit of spaces is detected by its total left fibration
statement: Use simplicial sets, spaces, weak homotopy equivalences and coherent colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the right join cone of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], left fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and their space-valued classification of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. Fix a universe $\mathcal W$ and a $\mathcal W$-small simplicial set $L$. Let $F:L^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ be a coherent diagram and let $p:Z\to L^{\triangleright}$ be a left fibration classified by $F$, with $\mathcal W$-small total simplicial set. Put $Z_0=Z\times_{L^{\triangleright}}L$. The following are equivalent: the coherent cocone on $F|_L$ induced by precomposition with the map $L\times\Delta^1\to L^{\triangleright}$ that splits each interval simplex into its initial $L$-vertices and final cone vertices is colimiting; and the inclusion $Z_0\hookrightarrow Z$ is a weak homotopy equivalence of simplicial sets. No filteredness or quasicategory hypothesis on $L$ is required, and $L=\varnothing$ is allowed.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.4.5, equivalence (1) with (3), printed pp. 219-220; cone conventions as in the relative construction in Lemma 5.5.4.13. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical theorem.

proof.text: Put $B=L^{\triangleright}$ and let $v$ be its cone vertex. The inclusion $j:\{v\}\hookrightarrow B$ is right anodyne in the sense of [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones]. Indeed, start from $\{v\}$; in increasing dimension $n\geq0$, for each nondegenerate $n$-simplex $\sigma$ of $L$ attach the $(n+1)$-simplex $\sigma\star v$ along $\Lambda_{n+1}^{n+1}$. This horn is exactly the union of the coned proper faces of $\sigma$, already present from lower dimensions; its missing face is $\sigma$. Thus the attachment adds precisely $\sigma$ and its cone. A degenerate face is already in a lower-dimensional stage. These pushouts, with all simplices of a fixed dimension attached together, exhaust $B$. For $n=0$ the horn is the final vertex $\{v\}$, so the orientation is right anodyne. For empty $L$, $j$ is the identity.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.4.5 and Corollary 3.3.4.6; explicit cone-vertex horn filtration

proof.text:
For every $\mathcal W$-small Kan complex $X$, apply the mapping-space assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones] to $j$, $F:B\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ and the constant target $X$. It gives an equivalence
$$e_X:\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal S_{\mathcal W})}(F,\Delta_BX)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}}(F(v),X).$$
This is actual restriction to $v$. The lemma allows arbitrary simplicial bases, so neither $B$ nor $L$ needs to be a quasicategory. The target infinity category and the diagram categories are formed in a universe containing $\mathcal W$.

source.place: Proposition 7.2.2.1, opposite dual, and Proposition 7.2.1.3; right-anodyne restriction of cocones

proof.text:
Define $H:B\times\Delta^1\to B$ simplexwise by retaining the initial vertices of the $B$-simplex where the interval coordinate is $0$, and replacing its final vertices where that coordinate is $1$ by $v$. If the retained part already contains $v$, the additional $v$-vertices are degeneracies of the same cone simplex. Restriction and repetition of vertices commute with this rule. Hence $H$ is simplicial, $H|_0=1_B$, $H|_1$ is constant at $v$, and $H|_{\{v\}\times\Delta^1}$ is constant. Composition with $F$ gives a coherent transformation $\tau:F\to\Delta_BF(v)$ whose component at $v$ is the identity. Write $\lambda=\tau|_L$, exactly the cocone specified in the statement. Composition with $\tau$ gives
$$u_X:\operatorname{Map}(F(v),X)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal S_{\mathcal W})}(F,\Delta_BX).$$
The composite $e_Xu_X$ is homotopic to the identity because $\tau_v=1_{F(v)}$. Step 2 therefore makes $u_X$ an equivalence. If $r_X$ denotes restriction from $B$ to $L$, the composite $r_Xu_X$ is the map $a\mapsto\Delta_L(a)\circ\lambda$, with its coherent composition homotopy, rather than an arbitrary equivalence between these spaces.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.4.5; agent expansion of the normalized right-cone cocone and restriction comparison

proof.text: By the cocone dual of the mapping-space criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], $\lambda$ is colimiting if and only if $r_Xu_X$ is an equivalence for every $X\in\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$. Since $u_X$ is an equivalence by step 3, this is equivalent to $r_X$ being an equivalence for every such $X$. This uses the mapping-space characterization of an initial object in the coherent cocone category, not merely a universal property on homotopy classes.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.4.5, condition (1), expressed via coherent cocone mapping spaces

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] first over $B$ and then over $L$. The constant target $X$ is represented by $B\times X\to B$ and $L\times X\to L$, respectively; pullback of $Z$ to $L$ is precisely $Z_0$ and classifies $F|_L$. A map $Z\times\Delta^n\to B\times X$ over $B$ has its first coordinate forced to be $p$, so projection to the second coordinate identifies its simplicial set of such maps with $\operatorname{Fun}(Z,X)$. Similarly the boundary mapping simplicial set is $\operatorname{Fun}(Z_0,X)$. The classification's compatibility with pullback identifies $r_X$, up to its specified coherent comparison, with precomposition by $i:Z_0\hookrightarrow Z$:
$$i_X^*:\operatorname{Fun}(Z,X)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(Z_0,X).$$
Both complexes are Kan by the same mapping-space assertion. In particular the comparison concerns the actual inclusion, not just two abstract spaces of the same homotopy type.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.1.2, covariant dual, with the coherent diagram comparison; mapping into constant left fibrations

proof.text: We verify the Kan-model hypotheses needed to test $i$ by these function complexes. Use [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] on $\mathcal W$-small simplicial sets. Every object is cofibrant and the fibrant objects are exactly the Kan complexes. With degreewise products as tensors, internal function simplicial sets as enrichment and cotensors, the tensor-cotensor adjunction is currying of maps of products. The simplicial model axiom follows from [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product]: lifting the induced mapping-space map against a horn is adjoint to lifting a fibration against the pushout product of a monomorphism with that horn. This product is anodyne. If the object-side cofibration is trivial, exchange the two product factors and use a boundary inclusion in the other factor; its pushout product is again anodyne. If the object-side fibration is trivial, the pushout product of a monomorphism with any boundary is degreewise a monomorphism, hence lifts against it. The horn and boundary characterizations in the Kan-model node give precisely fibrations, trivial in the two asserted cases. Thus [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] applies. For any simplicial set $A$ and Kan complex $X$ it identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(A,X)$ naturally with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}}(qA,X)$, where $q$ is Kan-model localization. It also supplies this identification's compatibility with precomposition. Fibrant replacement stays among $\mathcal W$-small simplicial sets.

source.place: Theorem 1.3.4.20 and Remark 1.3.4.16; Kan-model specialization with the simplicial axiom checked from the cited pushout-product theorem

proof.text: Let $\mathcal C$ be the infinity localization in step 6, a quasicategory, and let $\mathcal H=h\mathcal C$ be its homotopy category in the sense of [lem-coef-localization-homotopy-category]: edges modulo the homotopy generated by $2$-simplices with a degenerate short side, composed by inner $2$-horn fillers. We identify $\mathcal H$ with the category of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] whose morphisms are $\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,y)$, identically on objects, by sending an edge to its component. This is well defined: by the triangle clause of that node, a $2$-simplex with edges $u,v,w$ gives $[v][u]=[w]$, so a degenerate short side gives $[w]=[v]$ or $[w]=[u]$. It is surjective since every component is represented by an edge. It is injective because a $1$-simplex of the right-pinched $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,y)$ is a $2$-simplex whose edge $01$ is degenerate at $x$, a generating homotopy between its edges $12$ and $02$, so edges in one component are homotopic. Degenerate edges go to identities, and the triangle clause applied to an inner horn filler shows that composition is preserved. Under this isomorphism, precomposition by a morphism of $\mathcal H$ is $\pi_0$ of precomposition by a representing edge on mapping spaces, which depends only on the class, again by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition].

source.place: Proposition 3.3.4.5, condition (3); agent mapping-test argument using model-category saturation (Hovey Theorem 1.2.10(iv))

proof.text: The functor-category localization property in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] makes $q:N(\mathrm{sSet}_{\mathcal W})\to\mathcal C$ a coherent localization at weak homotopy equivalences. Apply [lem-coef-localization-homotopy-category] to conclude that $\gamma:\mathrm{sSet}_{\mathcal W}\to\mathcal H$ is its ordinary localization. The comparison is by the actual functor $\gamma$, so its image of $i$ is exactly the morphism represented by $qi$ in step 6. Universes are enlarged for the category of all $\mathcal W$-small simplicial sets and for ordinary target categories, without changing the universe of the test Kan complexes.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.4.5, condition (3); agent mapping-test argument using model-category saturation (Hovey Theorem 1.2.10(iv))

proof.text: We now show that $i$ is a weak homotopy equivalence if and only if every $i_X^*$ is an equivalence. The forward implication follows since localization inverts $i$, and step 6 identifies precomposition on mapping spaces with $i_X^*$. Conversely, take components of these maps. Every object of $\mathcal C$ is equivalent to a $\mathcal W$-small Kan representative by the fibrant replacement in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] and the localization comparison in step 6. Hence precomposition with $\gamma(i)$ is bijective on morphisms into every object of $\mathcal H$. Surjectivity for target $\gamma(Z_0)$ gives $g:\gamma(Z)\to\gamma(Z_0)$ with $g\gamma(i)=1$. Injectivity for target $\gamma(Z)$ applied to $(\gamma(i)g)\gamma(i)=\gamma(i)$ gives $\gamma(i)g=1$. Thus $\gamma(i)$ is an isomorphism. Since step 8 made $\gamma$ an ordinary localization, [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences] now implies that $i$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Neither total space was assumed fibrant.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.4.5, condition (3); agent mapping-test argument using model-category saturation (Hovey Theorem 1.2.10(iv))

proof.text: Steps 4 and 5 identify the colimit condition with the function-complex tests of step 9, proving both implications. All indexing sets and total spaces used in these tests are $\mathcal W$-small as assumed. If $L=\varnothing$, then $B=\Delta^0$, $Z_0=\varnothing$, and $Z$ represents $F(v)$. The tests say that $F(v)$ is initial in spaces, equivalently that $\varnothing\to Z$ is a weak homotopy equivalence; the same proof applies because the filtration in step 1 is empty and the boundary transformation space is terminal. No argument used filteredness or a quasicategory structure on $L$.
